findings.title: open item: zero-allocation equality fast path has no direct assertion
findings.evidence: The guarantee holds by reading the code: holds_one_bound returns on equal_to_text (comparing/service.rs:186) before it dereferences the LazyScratch (:191). DecisionWorkspace.select is now &mut LazyScratch<SelectScratch> (comparing/types.rs:31). That also makes the runtime predicate path lazy: predicates.rs passed &mut *self.state, which at base was deref-coerced to &mut SelectScratch and so initialised the scratch on every call. No comparing test asserts that scratch.select_scratch.0.get() is still None after an equality-only row. The only such assertion is an integration check that lives elsewhere (execution_runtime .../scratch_owner/test.rs:98).

findings.title: open item: two hash-chain probes over KeyIndex (pre-existing)
findings.evidence: table_reach/borrowed.rs:112-150 (IndexedRows::probe and next_match) and table_model/service.rs:169-210 (matching_stored) each hash a key, mask it into index.heads, walk index.next, compare hashes and observe the same three progress counters. This duplication predates the branch, which only moved IndexedRows from operator/contract/views.rs to table_reach. table_model already owns RepresentationInput and matching_stored, and table_reach already depends on table_model, so table_model is the stronger owner of the one probe.
